# runr Provider

Manage [RunR](https://runr.sh) projects, environment variables, custom domains, deployments, bindings, runtime plugins, workflow triggers, model services, hosted MCP servers, access control and branding.

Credentials come from the provider block, else `RUNR_API_URL` / `RUNR_TOKEN`, else the current context of the `runr` CLI (`runr login`).

## Example Usage

```terraform
terraform {
  required_providers {
    runr = {
      source  = "runr.sh/brf-tech/runr"
      version = "~> 0.5"
    }
  }
}

# Credentials: this block, else RUNR_API_URL / RUNR_TOKEN, else the current
# context of the runr CLI (runr login).
provider "runr" {
  api_url = "https://runr.example.com"
  token   = var.runr_token # runr tokens create terraform --preset terraform
}

variable "runr_token" {
  type      = string
  sensitive = true
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Optional

- `api_url` (String) RunR console or API URL, e.g. `https://runr.example.com`. Default: `RUNR_API_URL`, else the CLI context.
- `context` (String) Name of a `runr` CLI context to take the URL and token from (default: the current context).
- `poll_interval` (String) How often builds, deployments and domain checks are polled (Go duration). Default `2s`.
- `token` (String, Sensitive) RunR API token (`runr tokens create terraform`). Default: `RUNR_TOKEN`, else the CLI context.
